islandSpatial.identity: stationSpatial.ts supplies stable station IDs, purposes and perimeter slots. islandCharacter.ts arranges them from the topic-first research family and stable island identity; family neighbors remain consistent. Scene roads, focus routes, portraits and fallback share the result.
islandSpatial.geometry: StationArchitecture.tsx supplies nine recognizable base SVG building kinds with research-family pigments and instruments to guide, arrival, reading, Pixi texture baking and SVG fallback. Instruments are architectural exhibits, not live measurements. No new shipping raster assets.
islandSpatial.overview: islandOverview fits actual elevated terrain bounds. Pixi refits on resize without animation; selection frames the actual elevated station center.
islandSpatial.camera: Normal atlas departurePose is an in-memory bookmark discarded on reload. Stage rebuild and touched/restored resize preserve the pose; search entry is queued while a roster rebuild boots. Exploration boat pose stays separate.
islandSpatial.fallback: Same buildSceneGraph, station addresses and StationArchitecture geometry; independent SVG viewBox fitting, simplified terrain and separate claim controls. Does not claim pixel parity with Pixi.
islandSpatial.scope: General generated-island L1 and station-reading L2. The machine-curiosity sample retains its bespoke QFT and interiors.
islandSpatial.entry: Canvas, guide, wayfinder and SVG fallback selection approach a real building and show its entrance with a semantic room diagram. Explicit room controls enter or resume reading. Native canvas picking uses the actual graph/camera, matching press/release and at most 6px total travel; drag/cancel does not activate. SVG controls support Enter and Space. Closing reading retains the selected building and restores entrance-action focus; onward reading actions can open an available room directly.
islandSpatial.availability: Recorded material can expose research stations independently of ledger growth; a visit does not unlock knowledge.

reviewV3.dispositionScope: The three original corrections only: night action/link contrast, metadata moved into Background, and PRODUCT.md persistence. All resolved; not a fresh whole-surface approval.
reviewV3.scope: Documenter inspected current source and all nine supplied final captures; no new screenshots, UI edits, tests or detector run.
reviewV3.validation: Handoff reported earlier web415 and renderer160, then44 affected tests after visual correction; both typechecks and build passed again after the camera fix. The earlier full17-case E2E run passed16/failed1camera. All4 targeted post-fix E2Es passed: camera/private note26.6s, phone6.6s, no-GPU4.1s and world round-trip39.7s. The previous failure is resolved; no clean full17 rerun is claimed.
reviewV3.detector: One run only, /tmp/frontier-upgrade/v3-detector.json:21 advisory palette/type findings. Added repeated architectural pigments, corrected night-action roles and reusable reading roles. Local fallbacks, one-off effects and inherited special-purpose values were not promoted into global primitives.
reviewV3.limitations: No claim of commit, push, deployment, live AI quality or scientific validation; QA captures are not shipping assets.

questionWall.layout: Two columns, 18px gap; main and expanded sheet span both columns. One expanded sheet at a time. At 760px and below: one column, 14px gap, padding 18px instead of 22px.
questionWall.content: Deduplicated main and related question sheets disclose their existing rewrite, author and editorial/archive source context.
questionWall.note: Append selected question to the browser-local island note, preserve existing thoughts, avoid duplicate insertion and reject overflow past 1200 characters with a status message.
questionWall.sourceContinuity: The selected sheet text travels into the library; desktop question context opens, while mobile starts collapsed with a one-line preview. Its scope note labels references as island-level without a recorded question-specific correspondence. Returning retains sheet expansion. Carried context resets on island change.
questionWall.rooms: Workshop boundaries, gallery stakes and unfinished-garden context reuse existing depth material; no new claims, measurements or source summaries.

reviewV4.dispositionScope: The same reviewer resolved the one selected-question continuity and source-scope finding; remaining clear. All ten recaptures valid, no visible regression from the fix. Not a fresh full-product review.
reviewV4.scope: Documenter checked current source, final logs and capture file dimensions; no new screenshots, browser, tests or detector run.
reviewV4.validation: After review correction, web typecheck/build passed and v4-review-e2e.log records 4/4 passing. v4-review-capture.log records actual canvas entry, SVG keyboard entry and empty scoped question/night/mobile Axe results. Handoff separately reports renderer160, affected54, follow-up picking31, and initial full web415 passed/2timeouts followed by affected-file10/10retry; no clean whole-suite rerun claimed.
reviewV4.detector: One v4 run:19 palette/type advisories, no non-advisory findings. Reused family pigments and question-reading roles are intentional scoped extensions. No ignores added for incidental older colors or one-off effects.
reviewV4.limitations: Local evidence only; no commit, push, deployment, live AI quality or scientific validation. QA captures are not shipping assets; bespoke machine-curiosity remains separate.

buildingExploration.wayfinder: Station positions and coastline derive from the same scene graph as the landscape. Six optional family itineraries use available station addresses: anomaly, observation, arguments, method transfer, rules to tests, and feasibility limits. The dashed route and text list suggest reading order, not a scientific relationship or required sequence.
buildingExploration.diagram: BuildingPlan reuses actual material rooms and retained floor addresses at the entrance and in the reader. Court: questions and unfinished ideas; stacks: sources, data and results; forum: explanations and discussion; bench: methods and departure. These forms do not depict physical floor counts.

shapes.scope: Repeated diagram component conventions only; no global radius tokens or detector ignores.

buildingExploration.readingHistory: Entrance previews add no reading history. Explicit room reads record at most 30 UI addresses. Returning then selecting another room branches from the returned address. Closing retains the selected station; revisiting restores room and saved scroll, with zero only when no position exists.
buildingExploration.transientState: During the current island visit, preserve station, room, scroll, expanded question, source picks, open research desk and draft fields. Island changes reset navigation and drafts.
buildingExploration.comparison: Select two deduplicated existing references or editorial digests. Preserve original links and attribution; state when no digest is recorded. Fewer than two sources leaves available material readable without inventing a comparison.
buildingExploration.privateDraft: Whiteboard, workshop and unfinished garden collect an expectation, a falsifying observation and a next test. No AI execution or experiment is implied. The simplified-model launcher remains separate.
buildingExploration.persistence: Only explicit append transfers a research draft into the existing persistent browser-local island note. Preserve prior text, avoid duplicates and reject overflow beyond 1200 characters while retaining note and draft; no publication or scientific claim.
buildingExploration.nightReplay: Hidden whenever a building is selected, at its entrance or while reading.

reviewV5.dispositionScope: Reviewer opened all 11 valid captures and found no material visual or interaction defect. The sole finding was stale documentation; this pass corrects current rules. The final documentation review result is recorded in ../../docs/island-experience-v5-review.md.
reviewV5.scope: Documenter checked source, existing logs and capture dimensions and performed documentation integrity checks only; no browser, UI edits, tests or detector rerun.
reviewV5.validation: Final related tests 29/29 and targeted E2E 6/6. Handoff records web typecheck, data-import checks and production build exit 0; existing large-chunk warning remains. Capture log records five empty scoped Axe AA checks and matching page/viewport widths.
reviewV5.detector: One run, three advisory diagram radii and no non-advisory findings. 20px door, 24px court and 22px forum curves are intentional scoped component geometry; no ignores added.
reviewV5.preview: Handoff local preview PID 25095, port 5174; existing port 8788 local API with memory storage.
reviewV5.limitations: Local evidence only. No commit, push, deployment, live AI quality or scientific validation. QA captures are not shipping assets; bespoke machine-curiosity remains separate.

fieldStudy.rooms: Append workshop:field-study and library:field-study after existing floors, preserving prior addresses, material and order. Invitation, entrance and reader share the study address.
fieldStudy.compactIdentity: Only the study room uses a 64px minimum top bar, 72px portrait and 25px building title. At 760px and below: 56px, 56px and 23px.
fieldStudy.phoneFigure: Minimum 440px figure width inside a focusable horizontal panning container with a visible hint and left-anchored caption. Prose and wrapping controls stay within the page; buttons, range targets and disclosures retain 44px minimum height.
fieldStudy.persistence: Versioned browser-local state per island validates choice, finite stepped value and the 500-character draft. Explicit append alone transfers conditions, observation, question and source URLs to the existing 1200-character island note; preserve note and draft on full/duplicate outcomes. Storage failure limits state to the open study. Existing research-desk drafts remain transient.
fieldStudy.sourceReturn: Carry title, current conditions and the authored or suggested question to library:field-study, with a direct-study-source boundary. The previous reading address restores the apparatus. Other question routes keep their island-level boundary.
fieldStudy.mobileNavigation: Index and onward cues navigate through the same keyed mobile island entry, update the island hash and reset transient reading context. Only the selected island study state restores. English island title/main question use existing atlas translations.
fieldStudy.semantics: Ten subject-specific apparatuses use actual local calculation or identified source-based qualitative conditions. The coding example explicitly compares unknown-location binary flips and known-location erased values, not identical flips plus locations; classical parity does not simulate quantum states or thresholds.
fieldStudy.imageryMotion: Existing paper, mineral blue and scoped study ochre with text/geometry distinctions. No new generated product raster, shadow or decorative motion; direct SVG state updates do not require GPU rendering.

reviewV7.dispositionScope: Only the single material flip/erasure semantics fix is resolved. Not a new whole-surface review, scientific review or production-release approval; no approved comp or separate QUALITY BAR card was supplied.
reviewV7.captureScope: Producer and reviewer opened all 23 final QA images: 20 recaptures plus three k=3 channel/English captures. QA evidence only, not product assets.
reviewV7.validation: Handoff: 1249 workspace plus 22 root tests, recursive typecheck, projection/import and build passed; main fix batch then passed 435 web tests, typecheck/build and 12 main E2Es. No-WebGL entrance passed separately 1/1. Later semantics-only fix passed 9/9 affected tests, one build and the same 20 recaptures; three extra captures and zh/en k=3 UI assertions show 56 flip candidates and four erasure fillings. No later whole-suite run claimed.
reviewV7.accessibilityScope: Final/review capture logs report matching document widths, no page errors and empty scoped night, phone and English study Axe findings.
reviewV7.detector: One run, three advisories only: study h4 19px and two inherited #8A6A1E uses outside the apparatus. The h4 role is recorded; inherited pigment is not a global token. No ignores or second run.
reviewV7.documenterScope: Current source and supplied implementation/review records; documentation integrity checks only. No browser tests, build or fresh critique.
reviewV7.runtime: Vite 5173 and memory API 8787; existing disk database/catalog identity mismatch preserved. Existing large-chunk warning remains.
reviewV7.limitations: No new commit, push, deployment, persistent-database migration, real-user usability, whole-product accessibility certification, live AI quality or scientific validation.

narrative.overview:
Warm paper, mineral pigments, fine ink lines and serif question headings carry the existing atlas identity into readable research workspaces. The wider atlas keeps its illustrated world and shared shell. The collision surface pairs green water and recognizable question islands with a quiet paper desk for following a thought.

This scoped refresh records the implemented September 6 exploration redesign. The user authorized free inquiry, richer cross-domain encounters and motivation through curiosity, choice and observable changes in thinking. These choices replace the collision worksheet; they do not replace the wider atlas identity or establish a new global brand. Shared visual authority remains `../../packages/assets/src/tokens.css` and `src/global.css`; the scoped surface is defined by `CollisionOverlay.tsx`, `CollisionVoyageMap.tsx`, `collision.css` and `src/data/collisionThemes.ts`.

The generated-island extension carries a chosen question through a landscape, an identifiable research building and a readable source. Purpose-led wayfinding, an entrance with a semantic room diagram, explicit room entry and unfoldable paper questions extend the incumbent world. Six research families add instruments, pigments, stable settlement arrangements and optional reading itineraries while retaining each station's recognizable function. Its visual authority is `src/components/island/island-exploration.css`, `src/components/island/island-navigation.css`, `StationArchitecture.tsx`, `islandCharacter.ts` and `stationSpatial.ts`, alongside the shared tokens. This scope covers general generated-island L1 and station-reading L2; the legacy `machine-curiosity` sample retains its bespoke QFT flow and interiors.

The September 8 v7 field studies extend this established world through ten content-rich islands. Each workshop offers a subject-specific apparatus whose conditions change its diagram and observation, followed by a stated rule, research sources, limitations and a private follow-up question. This is a code-led extension of island → building → room, with no new visual world, approved comp or separate QUALITY BAR card. `src/components/island/field-study/` supplies its authored content, models, SVG figures and scoped styling; `GeneratedIslandScreen.tsx`, `StationInteriorDrawer.tsx`, `islandDepth.ts` and `src/components/mobile/MobileShell.tsx` integrate it into the existing places and return paths. The scientific inventory and source-reading scope belong to `../../docs/island-field-studies-v7-2026-09-08.md`.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and mineral accents, with green water distinguishing the exploration map from the writing desk.
Serif questions, sans-serif controls and notes, monospaced identifiers and raw records.
Recognizable islands and meaningful route states, with an equivalent route list.
Optional next moves and revisitable thoughts, without worksheet completion or external rewards.
Stable architectural identities and family details connect landscape, wayfinding, arrival and reading; source material remains distinct from editorial and personal interpretation.
Distinct teaching apparatuses make assumptions and their consequences visible, with sources and open questions connected to the same island.

rules.name: The Scoped Palette Rule
rules.body: Shared chrome uses semantic surface/text aliases for day/night changes. The collision surface uses its own day-paper and green-water colors; do not assume that the atlas night theme recolors it. Keep the collision additions scoped.

rules.name: The Route Meaning Rule
rules.body: Dashed routes are editorial catalog connections. Solid routes indicate recorded personal content, including a saved thought or retained legacy field; they do not mean a claim is established. Dotted plum routes are unverified AI proposals. Color reinforces these line styles rather than replacing them.

rules.name: The Island Accent Rule
rules.body: Generated-island controls separate text emphasis, filled-action background and foreground roles. Day uses shared azurite and raised paper; night uses the scoped light-blue accent with a dark foreground. Links and active room labels use the text role, while entry actions, selected purpose lenses and model launchers use the fill/foreground pair. Do not reuse a night link color as both a button fill and its text.

rules.name: The Family Pigment Rule
rules.body: The six `family-*` accents extend building art within generated islands: muted plum for open questions, mineral teal for observation, umber for knowledge commons, fired clay for method transfer, slate blue for models, and leaf green for living substrates. The accent repeats across roofs, question-wall trim and family instruments; it does not replace the accessible day/night action roles. Family character is also expressed through instrument silhouettes and semantic neighbors, never through color alone. These are research-family identities, not measurements or maturity scales.

rules.name: The Writing Size Rule
rules.body: The free-thought composer uses 14px text with line-height 1.8 on desktop and 16px on mobile. Its minimum height is 120px and it resizes vertically. Mobile search remains 13px in the current source; do not describe every mobile field as 16px.

rules.name: The Reading Hierarchy Rule
rules.body: Lead L1 with the question's title and question, then disclose background, domain, stage, cluster and provenance. In L2, show building identity, room purpose, material heading, readable body and source link in that order. Keep metadata subordinate to the question and source attribution attached to the material it supports.

rules.name: The Mobile Work Rule
rules.body: At 800px and below, show either the full-height map or the desk beneath the shared header. The map uses two columns of islands and natural vertical scrolling. Its single-row theme navigation scrolls horizontally; the strip and its buttons must not shrink, and every theme button keeps a 44px minimum height. Selecting an island or route opens the desk; returning restores focus to the originating map control, with a selected-theme fallback.

rules.name: The Island Mobile Rule
rules.body: At 760px and below, L1 is a naturally scrolling sequence: question, 360px landscape, entrance when selected, then wayfinding, the purpose guide and onward controls. The entrance uses automatic width and natural page height with non-sticky actions. L2 occupies the full safe-area-aware viewport, hides the landscape and turns room navigation into a non-shrinking horizontal strip above independently scrolling material. A carried question starts collapsed with a one-line preview; source comparisons stack vertically and draft fields use 16px text. Purpose lenses and room tabs have a minimum 44px height. The mobile atlas provides an actual “登岛探索” entry into the generated screen, with browser-local notes and the optional model workbench; it is not just a question-card preview.

rules.name: The Spatial Address Rule
rules.body: Terrain placement, purpose guide, selected building, walking path and camera share station identity. `stationSpatial.ts` supplies the station vocabulary and perimeter slots; `islandCharacter.ts` arranges them from research family and stable island identity. A specific topic takes precedence over its broad cluster, with a domain fallback. Both organic and courtyard terrain grammars use the well-spaced perimeter; family neighbors remain consistent as the entrance orientation varies. Scene roads, focus routes and the SVG fallback share the resulting order. Overview fitting uses the actual elevated terrain bounds. A selected station frames its actual elevated center; returning to overview refits the coastline. The SVG fallback uses the same graph and addresses, with its own viewBox fitting rather than a second island layout.

rules.name: The Study Figure Rule
rules.body: On phones, preserve diagram geometry at a minimum width of 440px inside its focusable, horizontally scrollable figure. Show the horizontal-pan hint and keep the caption anchored to the container's left edge. Controls wrap and prose stays within the reading panel; the page must not acquire horizontal overflow. Choice buttons, range targets and rule disclosures retain a minimum 44px height. The observation follows the controls in the mobile reading flow, while changing a condition updates the diagram immediately.

rules.name: The Surface Rule
rules.body: Preserve existing scene depth in the atlas. Within the collision map and desk, use paper tone, fine rules and cartographic contours to establish hierarchy.

rules.name: The Architectural Identity Rule
rules.body: Nine purpose-specific base SVG geometries are reused in the landscape, guide portraits, arrival note and reading header: the open question wall, shelved library, opposing-board debate hall, instrument terrace, sawtooth workshop, unfinished garden, exhibition hall, open discussion pavilion and harbor. Family instruments and pigments vary the base drawings while preserving station footprints and recognizable purpose. Geometry belongs to station kind and research family, not votes, visits or invented maturity. Pixi bakes these same SVG drawings into runtime textures; the no-GPU view renders the SVG directly. No new shipping raster assets were added for v3 or v4.

rules.name: The Inquiry Rule
rules.body: In the collision workspace, progress is a change in the visitor's question, interpretation or observation. Preserve free entry, optional tools, branching and return; do not turn the theme map or thought desk into a mandatory sequence or a reward ledger.

rules.name: The Building Entry Rule
rules.body: Canvas, guide, wayfinder and fallback selection approach a real building and expose its semantic room diagram. Keep room reading explicit, allow any available room, and retain the building identity and return path throughout reading.

rules.name: The Reading Return Rule
rules.body: Preserve room addresses and recoverable reading context during the current island visit. Keep the bounded UI history and temporary research drafts distinct from an explicit append to the persistent private notebook. A return path, visited-room label or reading itinerary is navigation, never a scientific result.

rules.name: The Material Boundary Rule
rules.body: Keep original citations, editorial explanation, recorded structure, model observation and private question visibly distinguishable. Spatial proximity, walking paths, building size and visits organize access; none is a scientific relation or a measure of research validity.

rules.name: The Study Evidence Rule
rules.body: A visible change must follow the stated teaching rule or an identified source condition. Keep its observation, the original finding, the model's limitation and the visitor's question separately readable. Sources and voluntary onward routes continue inquiry; they do not certify the model or complete the island.

dos: Do preserve the wider atlas identity, shared font stacks and existing shell authority.
Do keep the collision green-water map and paper desk as scoped surface decisions.
Do preserve stable island shapes, route line-style meanings and an accessible text route list.
Do keep free writing, optional model prediction, branching and revisiting available without completion gates.
Do preserve readable notes, visible focus and non-shrinking mobile theme controls.
Do distinguish catalog sources, local reading prompts, personal records and unverified AI proposals.
Do preserve one station identity across map, guide, arrival, reading and fallback.
Do keep purpose choices freely available, reading text legible in both themes, and source links attached to their material.
Do preserve a family's instrument identity and stable station arrangement across landscape, portraits and fallback.
Do carry the selected question into source reading, label island-level references accurately, and append private notes without overwriting them.
Do preserve study-specific calculations, stated assumptions, direct study-source addresses and private state when returning to an apparatus.
Do confine wide phone figures to their focusable panning container while keeping controls and prose within the page.
donts: Don't turn the collision workspace back into a required worksheet, stamp collection or completion counter.
Don't use island distance, elevation or a solid personal route as scientific validation.
Don't present an unconfigured AI partner, a local prompt or a simplified-model observation as a verified research result.
Don't apply the collision layout or palette to the wider atlas by assumption.
Don't treat architectural size, paths or visits as scientific evidence or a knowledge-unlock system.
Don't claim the generated-island extension replaces the bespoke machine-curiosity QFT flow.
Don't use family pigments, instruments, station availability or settlement proximity as a research measurement or maturity claim.
Don't flatten the ten studies into repeated cards, turn their index into a required course, or present a teaching output as a research finding.
